python -m pytest tests/visible/test_paging.py -q && python - <<'PY'
from repo.paging import num_pages, old_page_count
from repo.rows import page_summary

cases = [
    (0, 10, 0),
    (1, 10, 1),
    (9, 10, 1),
    (10, 10, 1),
    (11, 10, 2),
    (100, 10, 10),
    (101, 10, 11),
    (1, 1, 1),
    (7, 3, 3),
]
for total, per_page, expected in cases:
    got = num_pages(total, per_page)
    assert got == expected, (total, per_page, got, expected)
    assert old_page_count(total, per_page) == expected

assert page_summary(0, 10) == {"pages": 0, "first_page_start": None, "last_page_start": None}
assert page_summary(101, 10) == {"pages": 11, "first_page_start": 0, "last_page_start": 100}
assert page_summary(100, 10) == {"pages": 10, "first_page_start": 0, "last_page_start": 90}
assert page_summary(5, 10) == {"pages": 1, "first_page_start": 0, "last_page_start": 0}
try:
    num_pages(10, 0)
    raise SystemExit("expected ValueError")
except ValueError:
    pass
print("ok")
PY

content.text:
`num_pages` was using floor division, so a partial last page never counted. 101 rows at 10 per page came back as 10 pages instead of 11.

It now rounds up with ceiling division, and still returns 0 when there are no rows. `old_page_count` and `page_summary` both go through `num_pages`, so their page counts and the last-page start index follow the same rule. An empty export still reports no first or last page.

Visible paging tests pass, including the exact-multiple case (100 rows at 10 per page is still 10 pages).
